unit.title: Threat Models and a Tested Authorization Boundary
unit.scope: One self-contained software-engineering kickoff aligned with the catalog's systems-security themes; it is not a reconstruction of an MIT lecture or lab.
unit.learner_profile: Strong in algorithms and programming fundamentals; intentionally practicing requirements, trust boundaries, defensive interfaces, tests, and evidence-based debugging.
prerequisites: Comfort writing and testing Python programs
Basic process, file, and command-line concepts
Ability to reason from invariants and finite case partitions
learning_objectives: Turn an informal security goal into explicit assets, actors, trust boundaries, assumptions, and non-goals
Implement a small authorization policy with strict input validation and default-deny behavior
Separate untrusted-input parsing from a deterministic policy core
Derive table-driven examples and invariant tests from a policy rather than from implementation details
Record reproducible commands, failures, experiments, and limitations as engineering evidence
excluded_scope: Claims of completing MIT 6.858 or any official MIT lab
Network services, deployment, real credentials, or attacks on any live target
Reconstruction of unavailable lecture, lab, starter-code, or final-project material
Authentication, persistent storage, distributed consistency, and production deployment

required_evidence: A runnable local implementation and deterministic automated tests
A learner-authored threat model and answers to the comprehension prompts in notes.md
Reproducible commands and observed results in submission.md
Hypothesis, experiment, observation, and resolution entries in debugging-log.md
An independent examiner verdict grounded in the staged artifacts
completion_policy.on_unit_pass: Record only this kickoff unit as passed; keep the course in progress and make no transfer or whole-course claim.
completion_policy.later_expansion: A later deterministic job must separately classify, stage, and validate each additional unit and its materials. Missing source material may not be inferred from catalog prose.

provenance.preparation_basis: Only the supplied catalog snapshot was used as source data.
provenance.authorship_note: The kickoff task, learner documents, classifications, and rubric are newly authored preparation artifacts and are not represented as MIT course materials.
limitations: Catalog assertions were not independently verified against the linked course website.
No linked paper, course page, lecture, assignment specification, or starter repository was fetched.
The catalog descriptions do not provide enough material to reproduce any official lab.
